title: Replay verification handbook and short status attachment
summary: Short, attachable handbook for customers describing how to validate suspicious inference outputs, safely replay requests, and package evidence for support. Intended to accompany a concise status update on the public status page or a direct customer email.
statuspage_update_brief:
Title: Brief service irregularity affecting some structured outputs — investigating
Status: Investigating
Impact: A very small fraction of requests in EU and US regions returned unexpected or incomplete structured responses for a short window. Estimated affected requests: <0.1%.
Immediate action: We rolled back a recent routing tweak and applied targeted cache eviction.
Customer action: If you observed incorrect outputs, please follow the verification checklist below and open a ticket with our support team.
Contact: support@redwood.ai (include request-id from responses)
customer_postmortem_high_level: Overview: During a brief window a routing optimization interacted with warm connection reuse in a way that could return outdated prefix tokens for some streaming sessions. Root cause: an ordering issue in the routing decision path when a cache warm-up race occurred. Resolution: removed the optimization, invalidated affected caches, and added a guard in the routing controller to prevent serving unverified cache entries. Scope: limited, no data leakage. Next: rolling tests and additional telemetry to detect recurrence.
verification_checklist: Locate affected request timestamps and request-ids from your application logs
Pin the model and commit used at the time of the request to rule out model drift
Re-run a single example against the non-streaming endpoint to compare canonical output
If you normally stream, run the same input in streaming mode and capture the full event stream including final markers
Record token counts and compare for truncation versus content deviation
If differences remain, gather one representative request/response bundle and submit via the upload link provided by support
safe_replay_guidance: Start with one or two isolated requests; do not replay large volumes without contacting support
Use identical headers (model, model_version, region) to the original call when available
Disable client-side automatic retries while capturing replays to avoid masking or doubling behavior
Prefer non-production credentials or a test tenant for bulk replays
Capture the x-request-id response header on every replayed call and include it in evidence
evidence_format_requirements: Minimum: request timestamp, x-request-id, full request body (redacted if needed), full response payload, model_id and model_version
Helpful: SDK debug logs showing connection reuse, streaming fragment logs, client retry traces
Pack these files into a single gzip and upload using the secure link provided in your support ticket
commitments_and_timeline: Initial public note and short checklist: immediate (this attachment)
Targeted verification for submitted evidence bundles: within 48 hours of receipt
Follow-up technical summary for affected tenants: within 5 business days
Preventative control rollout (routing guard + telemetry): planned within 7 days pending validation
internal_guidance_for_sender: When attaching to a status update keep the top two paragraphs customer-friendly and include the single-example checklist. For enterprise customers offer a screenshare to walk through replay steps. Do not share internal incident tickets; use linked_artifacts to track internal references.
security_and_privacy_note: No customer payloads were exposed outside of normal serving. We only request minimal redacted payloads for debugging; customers with strict compliance can request an encrypted upload token and a scoped forensic replay under NDA.
notes_for_follow_up_actions: Engineering will add a unit/regression test that simulates warm-session reuse and a nightly probe that looks for unusually repeated prefix tokens across connections. Update linked_artifacts with final ticket numbers and attach the replay report when complete.
